Subject: EdgeCase AI — commit velocity and reprofile plan

Hi Maria,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. We dug into the telemetry you shared and combined it with our infra-side telemetry — there are two clear signals: a sustained 18% above-commit utilization on weekday peaks and a short-lived nightly burst pattern that could be absorbed by a small burst pool rather than permanent commit.

Proposal (high level):
- Convert 30% of your current burst allocation into steady commit (adds ~12 A100-equivalent GPUs) phased over 8 weeks.
- Preserve a 10% burst buffer for unpredictable spikes (auto-burst to a regional pool).
- Run a telemetry-led rollback window: if 2 consecutive weeks post-conversion show >10% underutilization, we automatically reprofile back to prior split.

Deliverables I can get to you by EOD Friday: a phased schedule, preliminary SOW language, and a pricing delta for the commit shift. Can you attach the utilization export (hourly) for the last 60 days so Karthik can run the kernel-aware fit?

Thanks — Hannah

> 
> Thanks — attaching our 60-day hourly export...

Hi Maria — thanks for the file, I ran a kernel-fit and came up with a conservative staging plan:

- Phase 0 (1 week): Validate per-model sequence-length distribution on the commit candidates (no change in capacity).
- Phase 1 (weeks 1–2): Move 40% of burst tokens to commit but keep a hot-standby pool for pre-warming — this maps to +8 A100-equivalent commit.
- Phase 2 (weeks 3–6): Incremental +4 A100-equivalent commit after monitoring 14-day P95 tail latencies and token-cost delta.
- Fallback: If end-to-end 95th latency degrades >15% or cost per token increases >8% for two sequential weeks, pause and auto-fallback.

Operational notes: we can do model pin-free transitions by leveraging the KV cache transfer and prefix caching during the handoff windows (we'll schedule low-traffic hours for the heavy reprofile steps). I attached an internal runbook excerpt as capacity_runbook_v2.pdf for ops details.
